{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts are systematically too high, especially at horizons beyond 10 days, requiring 2-3% annualization of predictions toward historical means.",
    "Sentiment momentum effects are real but decay rapidly - only sentiment changes within the last 3-4 observations should be directly incorporated into short-term forecasts.",
    "Forecasts exhibit excessive volatility relative to true outcomes, suggesting the model overreacts to noise; smooth predictions by 30-50% for horizons beyond 15 days.",
    "When sentiment turns negative (value < 0), model-under-predicts the bottom, suggesting a lag that fills in over the first 5-7 days of the horizon.",
    "Mean reversion bias exists but is asymmetric - model under-predicts during upticks more than it over-predicts during downticks, particularly when sentiment is positive.",
    "Cross-horizon correlation in predictions is too strong; true outcomes exhibit more divergence than model forecasts, especially after day 10 where uncertainty explodes.",
    "Sentiment strength matters nonlinearly - only sentiment deviations beyond ±0.5 have meaningful forecast impact; weaker signals should be attenuated"
] }
